# transformers.modeling_utils

## transformers.modeling_utils

- `Any(*args, **kwargs)` — Special type indicating an unconstrained type.
- `AttentionInterface()` — Dict-like object keeping track of allowed attention functions. You can easily add a new attention function with a call to `register()`. If a model needs to locally overwrite an existing attention function, say `sdpa`, it needs to declare a new instance of this class inside the `modeling_<model>.py`, and declare it on that instance.
- `Callable()` — class
- `CompileConfig(fullgraph: bool = False, dynamic: bool | None = None, backend: str | collections.abc.Callable = 'inductor', mode: str = 'reduce-overhead', options: dict | None = None) -> None` — Class that holds arguments relative to `torch.compile` behavior, when using automatic compilation in `generate`. See [`torch.compile`](https://pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.compile.html) for more details on the arguments.
- `ContextManagers(context_managers: 'list[AbstractContextManager]')` — Wrapper for `contextlib.ExitStack` which enters a collection of context managers. Adaptation of `ContextManagers` in the `fastcore` library.
- `DistributedConfig(tp_size: int | None = None, tp_plan: Union[dict[str, str], Literal['auto'], NoneType] = None, enable_sequence_parallel: bool = False, enable_expert_parallel: bool = False, fsdp_size: int | None = None, fsdp_cpu_offload: bool = False, fsdp_mixed_precision: bool = False, pp_size: int | None = None, ep_size: int | None = None, ep_plan: dict[str, str] | None = None) -> None` — Configuration for native distributed inference and training with tensor, pipeline, or FSDP2 parallelism.
- `DistributedMixin()` — Distributed orchestration and save/load hooks for [`PreTrainedModel`].
- `DownloadKwargs` — dict() -> new empty dictionary dict(mapping) -> new dictionary initialized from a mapping object's (key, value) pairs dict(iterable) -> new dictionary initialized as if via: d = {} for k, v in iterable: d[k] = v dict(**kwargs) -> new dictionary initialized with the name=value pairs in the keyword argument list. For example: dict(one=1, two=2)
- `EmbeddingAccessMixin()` — Base utilities to regroup getters and setters for embeddings. Introduces the `input_layer_embed` attribute, which indicates where the input embeddings come from and where they should be set.
- `GeneralInterface()` — Dict-like object keeping track of a class-wide mapping, as well as a local one. Allows to have library-wide modifications through the class mapping, as well as local modifications in a single file with the local mapping.
- `GenerationConfig(**kwargs)` — Class that holds a configuration for a generation task. A `generate` call supports the following generation methods for text-decoder, text-to-text, speech-to-text, and vision-to-text models:
- `HfQuantizer(quantization_config: transformers.utils.quantization_config.QuantizationConfigMixin, **kwargs)` — Abstract class of the HuggingFace quantizer. Supports for now quantizing HF transformers models for inference and/or quantization. This class is used only for transformers.PreTrainedModel.from_pretrained and cannot be easily used outside the scope of that method yet.
- `Iterator()` — class
- `KernelConfig(kernel_mapping=None, use_local_kernel=False, inherit_mapping=True)` — Kernel configuration class. This class is used to configure the kernel mapping for a model.
- `LoadStateDictConfig(pretrained_model_name_or_path: str | None = None, download_kwargs: transformers.utils.hub.DownloadKwargs | None = <factory>, use_safetensors: bool | None = None, ignore_mismatched_sizes: bool = False, sharded_metadata: dict | None = None, device_map: dict | None = None, disk_offload_folder: str | None = None, offload_buffers: bool = False, dtype: torch.dtype | None = None, dtype_plan: dict = <factory>, hf_quantizer: transformers.quantizers.base.HfQuantizer | None = None, device_mesh: 'DeviceMeshLike | None' = None, weights_only: bool = True, weight_mapping: list[transformers.core_model_loading.WeightConverter | transformers.core_model_loading.WeightRenaming] | None = None, disable_mmap: bool | None = None) -> None` — Config for loading weights. This allows bundling arguments that are just passed around.
- `LoadStateDictInfo(missing_keys: set[str], unexpected_keys: set[str], mismatched_keys: set[tuple[str, tuple[int], tuple[int]]], error_msgs: list[str], conversion_errors: dict[str, str], skipped_pp_keys: set[str]) -> None` — Mutable container for state-dict loading results and diagnostics. Each entry in this structure is mutable, and will usually be mutated in-place during the loading pipeline.
- `ModuleUtilsMixin()` — A few utilities for `torch.nn.Modules`, to be used as a mixin.
- `OutputRecorder(target_class: 'type[nn.Module]', index: 'int' = 0, layer_name: 'str | None' = None, class_name: 'str | None' = None, capture_initial_hidden_state: 'bool' = True) -> None` — Configuration for recording outputs from a model via hooks.
- `PeftAdapterMixin()` — A class containing all functions for loading and using adapters weights that are supported in PEFT library. For more details about adapters and injecting them on a transformer-based model, check out the documentation of PEFT library: https://huggingface.co/docs/peft/index
- `PreTrainedAudioTokenizerBase(config: transformers.configuration_utils.PreTrainedConfig, *inputs, **kwargs)` — Class that additionally defines the behavior of any `audio_tokenizer` to be added. Characteristic for any of them: 1. Encode raw audio into discrete audio codebooks (with x channels) 2. Decode from discrete audio codebooks back to raw audio It is possible that they can decode in different ways given a different representation but they are forced to support 2. nonetheless, e.g. see `DAC`.
- `PreTrainedConfig(transformers_version: 'str | None' = None, architectures: 'list[str] | None' = None, output_hidden_states: 'bool | None' = False, return_dict: 'bool | None' = True, dtype: 'str | torch.dtype | None' = None, chunk_size_feed_forward: 'int' = 0, is_encoder_decoder: 'bool' = False, id2label: 'dict[int, str] | dict[str, str] | None' = None, label2id: 'dict[str, int] | dict[str, str] | None' = None, problem_type: "Literal['regression', 'single_label_classification', 'multi_label_classification'] | None" = None) -> None` — Base class for all configuration classes. - `caching_allocator_warmup(model: transformers.modeling_utils.PreTrainedModel, expanded_device_map: dict, hf_quantizer: transformers.quantizers.base.HfQuantizer | None)` — This function warm-ups the caching allocator based on the size of the model tensors that will reside on each device. It allows to have one large call to Malloc, instead of recursively calling it later when loading the model, which is actually the loading speed bottleneck. Calling this function allows to cut the model loading time by a very large margin.
